title: Listening to Fletcher Henderson and Goldkette bands
summary: The Owls listened to Henderson and Jean Goldkette records; Netto recalls the steady swing feel on second and fourth beats.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, Louis went on to play with a band that seems to have had some influence on you guys and the ailes. Fletcher Henderson? Yeah, yeah. Did you listen a lot to Fletcher Henderson?

Yeah, we listened to Fletcher Henderson and that other band from Canada up there. What was the name of that? You know? Canada? I think they were, well, I don't know if they were Canadians, but they were playing up in Canada. Radio came in around 20- Is this a black group? No, I don't believe. I don't believe. Oh, Christ. Godfrey had some of these recordings over there. I thought they were terrific.
Was this before the Casa Luma was organized? Yeah, before Casa Luma. Before Gene Goldcat? That's the one. Gene Goldcat.
Gene Goldcat. Gene Goldcat. I thought that they were terrific.
Did they have a good bass player? Huh? Did they have a good bass player?
Well, I wasn't paying much attention to bass, but I was listening to the old band.
The bass player was from New Orleans, Steve Brown. Do you remember him? I heard of him.

I didn't know him. I heard of him. He left here before. He played with the rhythm keys. Yeah. But back in those days, they wanted to be steady and swing, you know, just a little emphasis on that third beat, on the second and fourth beat, rather. Yeah. And... Syncopation?
